newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX NIKKEI FUTURES END HIGHER BUT ON THIN VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX NIKKEI FUTURES END HIGHER BUT ON THIN VOLUME.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished higher on Thursday in line with gains on an underlying cash market boosted by buying of high-tech shares.
But dealers said the rise was not backed by strong volumes and the market might have trouble extending its gains.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract added 230 points to end at 19,275 on light turnover of 13,250 lots.
A trader at a U.S. futures house said the dollar's spike above 116 yen in afternoon trade helped lift the market.
She said the September Nikkei could head higher but resistance was likely around 19,500.
A senior dealer at a Japanese brokerage said the contract would probably consolidate in its recent 18,800-19,200 range for the time being.
"So far I cannot find any reason (for a rise). Everybody is waiting for fresh factors," he said. Volumes were likely to pick up next week when Japanese players returned from a summer break, he said.
Taiwan stock index futures ended higher as Taipei shares staged a technical rebound after three days of heavy falls. The August MSCI contract added 4.9 to 402.1 on volume of 2,291 lots.
